note: Biblical majuscule | Similar to Vindob. theol. gr. 31, Paris. suppl. gr. 1286, and Codex Purpureus Rossanensis, suggesting a date in the sixth century (501-600 CE) and a place of origin in the region of Syria or Antioch (cf. G. Cavallo, Ricerche sulla maiuscola biblica (Florence, 1967), pp. 98-104; P. Orsini, Manoscritti in maiuscola biblica. Materiali per un aggiornamento (Cassino, 2005), pp. 176-177, 201-203, 210-211

These folios preserve two sections of text (John 6:68-7:31 and 8:53-9:23), with an extensive gap between them (John 7:31-8:52). The missing text would have occupied about 18 columns (9 sides, i.e. 4 folios + 1 side). Codicologically more likely is the exclusion of the “Pericope Adulterae” (7:53-8:11). In that case, the missing text would have occupied about 16 columns (8 sides, i.e. 4 folios.). These four lost folios were the two central bifolios of the quire (if it was a quaternion)
